thought: looks before leaping

thought: notes the face for later

thought: not dumb muscle at all

thought: still not sat the tests

thought: a fine sword arm, not quite Imcando fine

thought: an honest look, like his squire's

thought: a sensible face for the parade crowd

thought: carries themselves like his father did

thought: someone who doesn't waste his time

thought: stood aside for a knight

thought: his sword has more edge than their wit

thought: Asrol brought it home unmarked

thought: pleased the knights have noticed the heirloom

thought: his father would be glad it's home

thought: busy armoury, but time for his blade

thought: in good spirits since the sword came home

thought: they look like someone who returns things

thought: fine, though not as fine as his sword

thought: reminds him of honest Asrol

thought: they'd march well

thought: a knight could do worse than walk like them

thought: his friends down the mine

thought: closest anvils to the mine, and still peaceful

thought: another pickaxe head finished, nicely tempered

thought: arms made for a pickaxe

thought: polite and unhurried, like the dwarves below

thought: a smith's patience

thought: a friendly face by his gate

thought: walks like a miner

thought: Nurmof likes polite customers too

thought: could carry six lumps of clay without grumbling

thought: a proper metalworker's look

thought: if they want a pickaxe, Nurmof's below

line: How nice that some folk have time to stroll about, traveller.

thought: iron's in the mine, should they feel useful
line: Iron ore's in the mine, traveller, should you ever feel useful.

thought: those arms and copper
line: Those arms would struggle with copper, never mind iron, I'd say.

thought: bring back clay if they trip on any
line: Off for a stroll? Bring back some clay if you trip on any.

thought: empty hands, empty anvils
line: Your hands are empty and so are my anvils. Funny old world.

thought: someone's fetching the clay
line: Clay should be along soon. Somebody's fetching it, bless them.

thought: cleared space for ore, hopefully
line: I've cleared a space for the ore. Hopeful of me, perhaps.

thought: copper is close by
line: Copper's easy found, just inside the mine. Shouldn't be long.

thought: iron wants practice; hopes the helper has it
line: Iron's the tricky one. I hope they've had their practice.

thought: Nurmof can wait
line: Nurmof can wait a day longer. I'll tell him so if he asks.

thought: the anvils idle while he waits
line: Anvils sat idle all morning. They're not used to it.

thought: casts out ready for clay
line: Kept the casts out. Won't need them till the clay comes.

thought: hears picks in the mine
line: Heard a pickaxe ringing in the mine. That'll be my helper, I expect.

thought: back quickly, good stride
line: Back already, traveller? You've a good stride for fetching ore.

thought: kind to take it on
line: Kind of you to take this on, traveller. Not many would.

thought: a miner in the making
line: You'll make a fine miner yet, traveller, mark my words.

thought: the dwarves below will take them for one of their own
line: That's the spirit! The lads below will take you for one of theirs.

thought: having a go at iron anyway
line: Iron's no small thing, and you're having a go anyway. Good for you.

thought: his anvils will be theirs soon
line: Those anvils will be yours to use soon enough, traveller.

thought: a helper with manners
line: A helper with manners! I'd almost forgotten there were such folk.

thought: already walks like a miner
line: You've a miner's walk already, traveller. Won't be long now.

thought: clay doesn't fetch itself
line: Clay doesn't fetch itself, traveller, much as I'd like it to.

thought: the mine is the big hole in the mountain
line: Still empty-handed? The mine's the big hole in the mountain.

thought: scenic route
line: Taking the scenic route to the mine, are we?

thought: iron trouble, as he said
line: Iron giving you trouble? It does want practice, iron.

thought: anvils used to waiting
line: No hurry, traveller. My anvils are used to waiting.

thought: buying the iron is allowed, he'll keep it quiet
line: If you'd sooner buy the iron, traveller, I'll not tell a soul.

thought: Nurmof is the one waiting
line: You're very welcome to dawdle, traveller. Nurmof's the one waiting.

thought: popping by between rocks
line: How kind of you to pop by between rocks, traveller.

thought: thinks he smells pie; it's the sea
line: Smell of pie on the wind, I'd swear. No, just the sea.

thought: the ice giant under the hut
line: That ice giant downstairs. Noisy neighbour, that.

thought: blurite's uses
line: Blurite. Good for a crossbow, useless for a sword.

thought: Wise Old Man's letter is late
line: Wise Old Man's letter is late. Should've sent a pie instead.

thought: keeping up with his ancestors
line: My ancestors smithed better than anyone. Least I can do is keep up.

thought: the cape is earned, then paid for
line: Cape's earned, not bought. Well, earned, then bought.

thought: cliff wind
line: Wind off the cliff gets in everywhere. Even the pie tin.

thought: master smiths should stick together
line: Smiths should stick together. Not many of us worth the name.

thought: good arms, wasted on fighting
line: Good arms, human. Wasted on fighting, mind.

thought: looks like they'd know good iron
line: Not bad. You look like you'd know a good bar of iron.

thought: baker's hands, the best kind
line: Baker's hands on you, human. Best sort of hands there is.

thought: smiths stick together; they look like one
line: Smiths stick together, my friend. You've the look of one.

thought: steady on the cliff path
line: Steady on your feet on a cliff path. That's something.

thought: not nosy
line: Decent sort, that one. Not one for nosy questions.

thought: a visitor who doesn't want a sword
line: By Guthix, a visitor who doesn't want a sword out of me.

thought: patience makes a smith
line: Patient look on you. Patience makes a smith.

thought: empty-handed, no pie
line: Empty-handed? Then what are you hanging about for?

thought: no anvil without pie
line: I'd not let you near my anvil, human. Not without a pie.

thought: takes them for a magic sort
line: Wave your stick somewhere else, human. This is a smith's cliff.

thought: won't fetch them back up the cliff
line: Mind the cliff edge, human. I've no time to fetch you back up.

thought: weak arms, and the giant
line: Arms like string. You'd not lift a lump of blurite.

thought: the walk of a pie-burner
line: That's the walk of someone who burns pies. I can always tell.

thought: adventurers never bring pie
line: Another adventurer. Never one with a pie.

thought: his ancestors would have laughed
line: My ancestors would have laughed you off this cliff, human.

thought: questions about his people
line: Questions, questions. Old dwarves are allowed their quiet.

thought: nobody brings pie any more
line: No pie through my door in an age. What's the world coming to?

thought: quiet on the cliff
line: Quiet on the cliff today. Suits me.

thought: won't talk about ancestors these days
line: Ancestors, ancestors. I don't talk about them, not these days.

thought: blurite under the hut, giant included
line: Bit of blurite under the hut, if you don't mind the giant.

thought: iron bars, but pie more
line: Could do with an iron bar or two. Could do with a pie more.

thought: Port Sarim, no decent pie
line: Port Sarim's handy enough for supplies. Not one decent pie in it.

thought: knights' swords used to match their post
line: Knights used to carry swords with proper designs on. Not now.

thought: decent, not nosy
line: You've a decent look, human. Not the prying sort, I'd say.

thought: smith's shoulders wasted
line: Smith's shoulders on you, human. Wasted on adventuring, I'd say.

thought: could be a smith if still
line: You'd make a fine smith if you'd sit still long enough.

thought: minds their own business
line: You mind your own business, human. More folk should.

thought: looks like someone who'd bring a pie
line: Good day, human. You look like someone who'd bring a pie.

thought: clever hands could temper a blade
line: Clever hands, by the look of them. Could temper a blade, maybe.

thought: didn't wobble on the cliff path
line: Fair play, you didn't wobble once on that cliff path.

thought: his ancestors would have fed them
line: Polite one, this. My ancestors would have fed them.

thought: anticipates a family question
line: If that's a question about my family, the answer's no.

thought: no pie, no talk
line: No pie, no talk. Simple rule, that.

thought: everyone wants swords, nobody brings pie
line: Everybody wants a sword off me. Nobody ever brings pie.

thought: never held a hammer
line: Never held a hammer in your life, have you, human?

thought: too old for visitors without pie
line: Too old for visitors, me. Specially ones without pie.

thought: the giant is friendlier
line: Mind the giant on your way down. He's friendlier than me.

thought: snooping round his hut
line: Snooping round an old smith's hut? Nothing here but iron and crumbs.

thought: can't tell iron from tin
line: Bet you can't even tell iron from tin, human.

thought: everyone asking about old swords now
line: Folk asking about old swords now. Never rains but it pours.

thought: knights' swords had to match their post
line: A knight's sword had to match his post, back then. Fussy lot.

thought: still thinking of a good pie
line: Had a decent pie lately. Still thinking about it.

thought: always short of iron bars
line: Need iron bars. Always need iron bars.

thought: blurite for hilts
line: Blurite's no use for a blade, but it dresses up a hilt nicely.

thought: why the sudden interest in his family
line: Why's everyone after my family history all of a sudden?

thought: cold work under the cliff
line: Cold work, fetching from under the cliff. Ice giant doesn't help.

thought: one more pie might jog his memory
line: One more pie and I might start remembering things. Might.

thought: they ask about swords politely
line: You're the one asking about swords. Polite about it, too.

thought: persistence suits a smith
line: Persistent, aren't you? Good quality in a smith.

thought: they've kept at it past the cliff
line: You've stuck at it, human. Most give up after the cliff.

thought: if that's pie, favourite visitor
line: If that's pie I smell, you're my favourite visitor.

thought: good manners and good legs
line: Good manners and good legs for a cliff. You'll do, human.

thought: they ask nicely
line: You ask nicely, I'll give you that. Most just shout.

thought: patient visitor
line: By Guthix, a visitor who can be patient. You'll go far.

thought: good at errands, somebody's lucky
line: Fair hand at errands, that one. Somebody's lucky.

thought: asking again; bring pie
line: Still asking about swords? Ask with a pie next time.

thought: not a sword shop
line: I'm not a sword shop, human. I'm a smith with a cliff.

thought: worse than the ice giant
line: Back again? You're worse than the ice giant.

thought: questions wear out an old dwarf
line: Questions, questions. You'll wear an old dwarf out.

thought: errands for some knight
line: Running errands for some knight, are you? Sounds about right.

thought: wants a sword and brought nothing
line: You want a sword out of me and you've brought nothing? Funny one.

thought: climbs like a squire, all elbows
line: You climb like a squire, human. All elbows.

thought: iron bars don't grow on the cliff
line: Don't stand there gawping. Iron bars don't grow on the cliff.

thought: master smith, and folk ask directions
line: Master smith of Misthalin, and folk still knock for directions.

thought: rune platemail is for heroes
line: Rune platemail's for heroes. Not for any fool wi' coin.

thought: another fancy-pants from the Guildmaster
line: Another fancy-pants from the Guildmaster, I'll wager. Always is.

thought: folk call him odd
line: Folk call me odd. Odd's better than chatty.

thought: Wilderness up the road, yet they come here
line: Wilderness just up the road, and they still come here for trouble.

thought: Edgeville was Ghost Town once, quieter
line: Ghost Town, they used to call this place. Quieter then, I'll bet.

thought: a master smith charges what he likes
line: A master smith charges what he likes. That's the point of being one.

thought: his own bulky plate keeps the wind off
line: Me own plate's bulkier than most. Keeps out the cliff wind.

thought: better manners than the Guildmaster's lot
line: Ye've better manners than most the Guildmaster sends.

thought: not much swagger
line: Not much swagger on you. I'll grant you that much.

thought: smith's arms
line: You've a smith's arms, I ken tell.

thought: quiet sort suits him
line: Quiet sort, you. Suits me fine.

thought: hasn't asked for armour
line: Least you've not asked me for armour yet. Good start.

thought: walks like someone who has done things
line: Hmph. You walk like somebody who's done more than talk.

thought: a visitor who doesn't prattle
line: A visitor who doesn't prattle. Makes a change, that.

thought: not one of the Guildmaster's peacocks
line: Not one of the Guildmaster's peacocks, are ye?

thought: swagger won't stop a dragon
line: Swagger like that's no use against a dragon, adventurer.

thought: rune platemail? not for them
line: Rune platemail, for you? Heroes only, adventurer.

thought: fancy talk gets nowhere here
line: Fancy talk won't get ye far round here.

thought: dragon questions go to the Guildmaster
line: Don't ask me how to kill anything. That's the Guildmaster's job.

thought: Edgeville full of would-be heroes
line: Edgeville's full of would-be heroes. Ye're no different.

thought: goblins have more sense
line: I've met goblins with more sense, adventurer.

thought: prices go up for starers
line: Prices go up for folk who stare. Mine do, anyhow.

thought: the Wilderness is that way
line: Wilderness is just up the road, if ye're bored. Do us both a favour.

thought: nothing to sell to passers-by
line: Nothing to sell to the likes of passers-by. Leave a man be.

thought: the Guildmaster's sent another, he can feel it
line: Guildmaster's sent another one my way, I'd wager. Can feel it.

thought: wants a quiet hut
line: Just want a quiet hut and a hot forge. Too much to ask?

thought: heroes without a dragon between them
line: Heroes, they call themselves. Not a dragon between 'em.

thought: rune plate waits for a real hero
line: Rune plate sits on me rack till a real hero comes.

thought: odd folk get left alone
line: Odd, they call me. Odd folk get left alone, mostly.

thought: Grand Exchange sells all but his armour
line: Grand Exchange sells everything, they say. Not my armour, it don't.

thought: cliff behind, fools in front
line: Cliff behind me and fools in front. 'Tis a hard life.

thought: hasn't asked for his armour
line: You've not asked for my armour. Wise, that.

thought: manners, at least
line: Manners, at least. More than the last one had.

thought: could swing a hammer
line: You look like you could swing a hammer, adventurer. Can ye?

thought: might be something in them
line: Might be sommat in you after all. Might.

thought: short visit, he likes those
line: Short and to the point, you. I like a short visit.

thought: less swagger than usual
line: Less swagger than the Guildmaster's usual lot, I'll grant.

thought: could be a hero deep down
line: Steady eyes on that one. Could be a hero in there, somewhere.

thought: took them for a fancy-pants, corrects himself
line: Thought you were another fancy-pants. No... you'll do.

thought: no hero in sight
line: Rune platemail's for heroes, and I don't see one.

thought: Guildmaster sent them, of course
line: The Guildmaster sent ye? Course he did.

thought: not slain so much as a chicken
line: Hero, that one? Not slain so much as a chicken, I'd wager.

thought: leave him be
line: Leave a man be, adventurer. I've nothing for the likes o' you.

thought: chatter belongs in Varrock
line: Want chatter? Varrock's down the road, not here.

thought: he'll believe it when he sees a dragon's head
line: Fancy-pants hero, are we? I'll believe it when I see a dragon's head.

thought: prove something before staring at his hut
line: Go prove something first, then come and stare at my hut.

thought: needs more than talk to wear his plate
line: You'd need more than talk to wear my plate. A dragon, say.

thought: told them: dragon first, then platemail
line: Told 'em: slay the dragon of Crandor, then we'll talk platemail.

thought: quiet now they've gone dragon-hunting
line: 'Tis quiet now they've gone dragon-hunting. Long may it last.

thought: wonders if they've been eaten
line: Wonder if that last one's been eaten yet.

thought: dragon questions go to the Guildmaster
line: Guildmaster can answer the dragon questions. Not me.

thought: platebody polished and waiting, maybe long
line: Platebody's polished and waiting. Might wait a long while.

thought: he isn't hard, just particular
line: Folk think I'm hard. I just like me armour on folk who've earned it.

thought: a dragon for a platebody is fair
line: A dragon for a platebody. Fair trade, by my reckoning.

thought: he'll eat his words if they return
line: If they come back wi' the dragon slain, I'll eat my words.

thought: still alive; Crandor hasn't had them
line: Still in one piece? Crandor hasn't had you yet, then.

thought: they took it on
line: You went and took it on. Didn't think ye would.

thought: more spine than most
line: More spine on that one than most the Guildmaster sends.

thought: a hero in them yet, maybe
line: Aye, there might be a hero in you yet. Might.

thought: not run off yet
line: Not run off yet. That's sommat.

thought: keep their head; platebody waits
line: Keep yer head on, adventurer. Platebody's waiting.

thought: they look like they have a plan
line: You've the look of someone with a plan. First one I've seen.

thought: less swagger since the dragon was mentioned
line: Bit less swagger on you since I mentioned that dragon. Good.

thought: the dragon is on Crandor, not here
line: Dragon's on Crandor, not in Edgeville. Ye might've noticed.

thought: back already, lost nerve
line: Back already? Lost your nerve, have you?

thought: staring won't change the terms
line: No platebody till the dragon's dead. Staring won't change that.

thought: not their nursemaid
line: Ask the Guildmaster how to kill it. I'm not yer nursemaid.

thought: alive, so not been to Crandor
line: Still alive, so ye've not been to Crandor yet.

thought: all talk and no dragon
line: All talk and no dragon, adventurer. Same as the rest.

thought: that face won't scare a dragon
line: Ye'll need more than that face to scare off a dragon.

thought: cold feet
line: Cold feet, is it? Crandor's not getting any closer.
